Command: Leaven shall not be seen in your borders during Passover
Summary: During Unleavened Bread, no leaven may be seen anywhere within Israel's borders, not only in the house.
Commandment: Let no leaven be seen in all your borders during the seven days.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The wider boundary extended the clean break from leaven beyond the house to the whole land's feast observance. Debated: some see the commanded observance fulfilled as shadow (Colossians 2:16-17); others keep feasts voluntarily as memorial, not as binding command. The site does not settle whether observance continues.
Purpose: Scripture's stated context: the meal is eaten in haste on the night of deliverance from Egypt, ready to depart (Exodus 12:11).
